characterization_methods: Laser detection of radius of curvature
evidence: Spectroscopic ellipsometry mapping of 49 points with 3 mm edge exclusion was used to measure film thickness on 200 mm wafers. Film composition was determined by Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy (RBS) and hydrogen forward scattering spectroscopy (HFS). Film composition depth profile was analyzed by secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS). Chemical state of the aluminum oxide films was analyzed by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The formation of interfacial layers was investigated using cross section transmission electron microscopy (TEM) on Si wafers that had hydrofluoric acid (HF)-last surface preparation prior to the Al2O3 deposition. Film surface morphology was studied by atomic force microscopy (AFM). Metal impurity analysis of the films was conducted using the HF vapor phase decomposition (HF-VPD) technique. Particle adders were measured optically by light scattering. Film stress as a function of temperature was measured on 50-nm-thick films from the change in Si substrate bow using laser detection of radius of curvature during an anneal up to 900 °C with a temperature ramp rate of 4 °C/min. Leakage currents were obtained using the HP4145B parameter analyzer. EOT was measured using a HP4275 LCR meter at a frequency of 10 kHz.
